craft_notes: Sthāyin: ease-joy (release easy). Sanskrit first: long compound qualification + easy predicate → L4 keeps the sweep line 1, ease line 2. Rows: row 2 (the long compound uncut — the sweep IS the verse). Rupture: dash after grasp — sweeping done, ease stated. Close: end-weight on hand (ease at hand). Minimal pass: dash for L3 comma. Read aloud: one long sweep, then easy. Rejected: splitting the compound — killed: easing what Sanskrit packs; 'luck' for lakṣmī — killed: fortune kept (Lakṣmī-register).

lines: Whose single mind sweeps clean the grasped-and-grasp,
grounded in self, release lies easy to his hand.
l4.sanskrit_cite: grāhyagrahaṇasaṃskāratiraskāraikacetasām / yogināṃ svātmaniṣṭhānāṃ mokṣalakṣmīr na durlabhā

reads_against.argmap: For yogins grounded in own self, release's fortune is not hard to win.
